intent: To demonstrate that eyewitness misinterpretation is the leading cause of wrongful convictions.

units.meaning: Eyewitness misinterpretation is the leading/highest cause in the chart, with value 72 (relative_value 0.72, i.e. 72%).
accepted_routes: Eyewitness misinterpretation is the leading cause at 72%.
72% of the cited exonerations involve inaccurate eyewitness testimony.
The eyewitness bar is highest, at about 72%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The eyewitness-misinterpretation bar must be visibly the tallest and must be labeled or annotated with 72% or 72.
units.temporal_anchor: The main evidence clause about inaccurate eyewitness testimony.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the exact top value 72%, or is 'leading cause' alone sufficient?

units.meaning: Eyewitness misinterpretation is greater than every other listed cause: 72 vs improper forensics 47, false confessions 27, and informant 15.
accepted_routes: Eyewitness misinterpretation tops all other listed causes.
No other listed cause reaches the eyewitness misinterpretation level.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The eyewitness bar must be shown alongside the other three bars at lower heights, with values or labels visible enough to compare.
units.temporal_anchor: The main evidence clause about eyewitness testimony being involved.
units.reviewer_question: Is it enough to compare eyewitness to all other causes, or must the runner-up gap also be explicit?

units.meaning: The full descending order is eyewitness misinterpretation 72, improper forensics 47, false confessions 27, informant 15.
accepted_routes: The bars descend from 72 to 47 to 27 to 15.
Eyewitness leads, then improper forensics, then false confessions, then informant.
Improper forensics is second at 47, followed by false confessions at 27 and informant at 15.
units.visual_evidence_rule: All four bars must appear in the correct order or be visibly sortable as eyewitness > improper forensics > false confessions > informant.
units.temporal_anchor: The visual reveal of the full bar series after the opening claim.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video show the complete ranking, or is the leading-cause comparison alone sufficient?

units.meaning: Eyewitness misinterpretation exceeds the second-ranked cause, improper forensics, by 25 percentage points: 72 − 47 = 25.
accepted_routes: Eyewitness misinterpretation leads improper forensics by 25 points.
The runner-up, improper forensics, is 25 points lower.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The top two bars must be visible with their values 72 and 47, plus a gap annotation or label showing 25.
units.temporal_anchor: The comparison beat immediately after the top two bars are introduced.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 25-point lead over the runner-up required, or is it optional enrichment?

units.meaning: Eyewitness misinterpretation is more than twice false confessions: 72 / 27 ≈ 2.7 times.
accepted_routes: Eyewitness misinterpretation is about 2.7 times false confessions.
False confessions is less than half the eyewitness level.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The eyewitness bar 72 and false-confessions bar 27 must be visible, with an annotation or scale indicating a greater-than-twofold difference.
units.temporal_anchor: An optional comparison beat after the main ranking is established.
units.reviewer_question: Does an extra magnitude comparison beyond the top ranking add value, or is it distracting?

optional_valid: Improper forensics is the runner-up at 47%.
False confessions is 27% and informant is 15%.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not claim the four listed values sum to 100% or build a pie chart; 72 + 47 + 27 + 15 = 161, and causes may overlap.
Do not say eyewitness misinterpretation causes 72% of all wrongful convictions; the table/narration context is DNA exonerations and involvement, not sole causation.
Do not claim 72% of cases are solely due to eyewitness error.
Do not introduce external thresholds or denominators that are not present in the table.
notes: Values are treated as percentages because value/relative_value pairs are 72/0.72, 47/0.47, 27/0.27, and 15/0.15. The minimal required claim is that eyewitness misinterpretation is the highest listed cause; full ranking and extra magnitude comparisons are optional enrichments.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
